name: Emre Kaya (synthetic)

facts.label: mechanical engineering
facts.story: Designs housings and impellers for industrial pumps and takes part in the prototype tests.

facts.label: fluid mechanics
facts.story: Checks flow behaviour of every redesign so that a stronger part does not cost efficiency.

facts.label: computer simulation
facts.story: Runs finite element and flow simulations to find stress peaks before a prototype is made.

facts.label: 3D modelling
facts.story: Models components in SolidWorks and keeps the drawings and revisions in the PDM system.

facts.label: design engineering components
facts.story: Redesigned a cracking pump housing with a larger internal radius and a thicker wall.

answers.recent_work: I'm a mechanical design engineer at a company that makes industrial pumps. I design components, run flow and strength simulations, and go down to the workshop when a prototype doesn't behave. I've been there nine years, after my master's here in Finland. I'm Muslim and fast in Ramadan, so I plan my heavy simulation runs for the evenings that month, and nobody has ever had a problem with it.
answers.example: We had a pump housing that kept cracking near the outlet during pressure tests. I built a finite element model, saw a stress peak at a sharp internal corner, and redesigned it with a larger radius and a slightly thicker wall. Then I checked the flow again to make sure the change didn't hurt the efficiency. The new housing passed the pressure test on the first try.
answers.tools: SolidWorks for 3D modelling and drawings, Ansys for strength and flow simulations, MATLAB for scripts when I need to process test data. We use a PDM system for revisions. In the workshop I use calipers and a coordinate measuring machine for critical dimensions, and I can read the shop's CNC programs.
answers.people: I'm in a design group of seven. I work with the test engineers who run the pressure and performance tests, and with purchasing about suppliers' tolerances. Sales sometimes bring me customer questions directly. I own the design of the housings and impellers, and I review the drawings of the newer people in the group.
answers.beyond: I wrote my thesis on cavitation in pumps, so I know the theory well enough to explain it. On the side I've built a small 3D printed test rig at home for flow experiments, and once a year I give a guest lecture on simulation at my old university.
answers.open_floor: Maybe that I like documenting the reasoning behind a design. Six months later nobody remembers why a radius is what it is.
answers.looking_for: Mechanical design or simulation work, product development in the machine or energy industry. English or Finnish both work. I'd prefer hybrid. My notice period is three months.

probes: The simulation work: I meshed the housing with finer elements around the corner, applied the test pressure, and compared the peak stress to the material's yield limit. The first version was above the limit, and the new radius brought it comfortably under.
When the first prototype leaked at a flange, I went down to the workshop, measured the flange face and found it was slightly out of flat. We changed the machining order and the leak was gone.
